events.title: The death of Pope Gregory XI
events.shortBlurb: The pope who ended the Avignon exile and brought the papacy home to Rome died there, on the eve of the Great Western Schism…
body: Pope Gregory XI died at Rome on 27 March 1378, aged about forty-nine, little more than a year after bringing the papacy home from Avignon. Born Pierre Roger de Beaufort about 1329, a nephew of Clement VI made a cardinal at eighteen, he had been elected pope at Avignon on 30 December 1370, the seventh and last of the Avignon popes.

Pressed by the letters of Catherine of Siena and by the entreaties of the Romans, he left Avignon on 13 September 1376 and, sailing from Marseille and up the Tiber from Ostia, made his solemn entry into Rome on 17 January 1377, ending nearly seventy years of exile from the apostolic see.

His death forced the conclave that, under pressure from a Roman mob, elected Urban VI within weeks; before the year was out the French cardinals had repudiated that choice and elected a rival, Clement VII, at Fondi, who established himself at Avignon the following year. The return Gregory had achieved thus opened the door to the Great Western Schism.
